title: On average about a third of a seen creator's words are coded as a claimed voice, mostly embodied, and about a third as the creator's own voice
caption: Each row: the creator-balanced mean share of a creator's words in the voice, with its 95% creator-bootstrap interval (2,000 draws). The middle model on the middle-model subset (178 recordings: two per creator chosen by a hash, plus the 41 recordings of the gate sample) is primary for voice; the small model is shown beside it on the same subset and on all 1,293 seen recordings. Voice sides under rule B with the primary (broad) own-voice definition; claimants are not restricted. Relayed voice alone is below the reliability floor (its two-model agreement failed its gate) and carries no claim. Exploratory (registry A2); not a test of H1-H10.

title: About one in five of a creator's read forecast candidates is a world-future statement (F1); listener-directed and non-future readings are each about one in four

Candidates without a valid answer after two attempts rest on fewer than 5 creators and are pooled with the smallest class (F8, reported only) by the plan's rule. All 1,293 seen recordings of the 71 seen creators; each creator's value is a share weighted by inverse inclusion probability (verified statements only, duplicates removed), and the mean is creator-balanced over the creators with any item in the base. title: Recognized speech covers about three quarters of the first 15 s and only half of the last 15 s of a recording

title: Between a fifth and three quarters of each measure's variance lies between creators; the recognizer's log-probability measures have the lowest share and the widest intervals
caption: Share of variance between creators (one-way random-intercept ICC) for ten word and timing measures (a) and six recognizer measures (b), all on the same 71 seen creators and 1,211 recordings (MATTR 1,106), each on the scale named in brackets: raw (open) and adjusted for log length, edition and median word probability (filled), with 95% creator-resampling bootstrap intervals; grey bars: the raw ICC's 95% parametric-bootstrap interval, for comparison only; triangles: raw with the artefact filter off. Pace 0.58 (0.47 to 0.66), share of time without speech 0.55 (0.41 to 0.67), contractions 0.72 (0.57 to 0.77), repeated five-word share 0.37 (0.26 to 0.46); the earlier draft's mean segment log-probability 0.40 (0.15 to 0.63); mean ln word probability per word 0.21 (0.06 to 0.53). For counts the ICC depends on the scale (first-person singular: 0.28 on the raw rate, 0.46 on the log rate, 0.53 on the negative-binomial latent scale). The ICC is a design fact of this roster. Interval level: 95% creator bootstrap. Exploratory, paper review (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

title: No seen recording has a reference known to be made by people; the run's recognizer and platform automatic captions disagree on about 4 words in 100
caption: Each row compares the run's recognizer text (re-made with the run's English-only model and settings) with another text of the same seen recording: dots are the creator mean (each creator once) and the word-pooled disagreement, lines their 95% percentile intervals from 2,000 creator-bootstrap resamples. Disagreement is substitutions, deletions and insertions over the reference words, after the normaliser wa-norm-v2, which was chosen after the result (version 1 is printed beside it in the table without rates, with counts and the share without disagreement only: beside version 2 each version-1 row differs in fewer than 5 creators). Every row is agreement of two machines, not an error rate: no seen recording has a reference known to be made by people, and the hold-out and other-group part (BR-b-H) was not run because fewer than 5 creators in each group have a reference that could be made by people. Base: 11 recordings of 11 creators with platform automatic captions; 48 recordings of 34 creators with the project's earlier text of the same recognizer and settings; 5 recordings of 5 creators with the project's earlier text of the larger multilingual model (a row added after the exploratory reporting plan); the undeclared transcripts rest on fewer than 5 creators and the pooled row of automatic texts is not published. Recognizer output, not checked by a person. Exploratory (registry A2); not a test of H1-H10. Made after a hold-out contact on 2026-11-22 (a text search that showed file names only).
